channel.title: Blockheight
channel.description: Blockheight reports crypto news: Bitcoin and Ethereum, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, regulation, security incidents and market structure.

item.title: XMR-to-Sepolia transfers need at least 10 Monero confirmations
item.description: ZeroFi’s XMR-to-Sepolia route requires 10 Monero confirmations, so the chain alone can take about 20 minutes; bridge processing and Sepolia delivery add variable time.

item.title: Why TRON Swap Liquidity Providers Can Lose Value
item.description: TRON swap LPs can finish with less value than holders when token prices diverge; pool mechanics, fees and price ranges determine whether providing liquidity pays.

item.title: How to Compare TRON USDT Swap Routes
item.description: Compare TRON USDT routes by net output, pool depth, slippage and network resource cost; a better quote can still leave less after fees when you execute.

item.title: How an Account Abstraction Wallet Handles a Bridge Route
item.description: An account abstraction wallet can package approvals and bridge calls, but each route still depends on chain support, fees, liquidity and destination settlement.

item.title: Cross-chain batching cuts wallet steps, not chain settlement
item.description: Cross-chain batching groups wallet actions into fewer transactions, but each chain still settles separately and may require its own approval and fee.

item.title: How treasury teams reconcile Manta Bridge transfers
item.description: Treasury teams can reconcile Manta Bridge transfers by matching both chains’ records, treating pending withdrawals as in transit and separating network fees.

item.title: Set a token spend limit before swapping from your wallet
item.description: A token approval lets a swap contract spend tokens from your wallet. Set a cap for the trade, then review any allowance left behind after the swap.

item.title: How to limit price risk when bridging XMR
item.description: An XMR bridge can expose a transfer to price moves before the swap settles. Control that window with quote checks, smaller transfers or a temporary hedge.

item.title: TRON swap permissions: how to spot unusual requests
item.description: A TRON swap may request a token allowance or contract call. Check the spender, amount, network and method before signing, then review access you no longer need.

item.title: A TRON USDT swap needs Energy, with TRX as backup
item.description: A USDT swap on TRON runs through smart contracts that use Energy; TRX can cover a shortfall, while staking or delegated resources can reduce the burn.

item.title: XMR Bridge Key Rotation Limits Reserve Signer Risk
item.description: Key rotation limits how long reserve signers stay exposed, but protecting XMR also requires multisig, verified migration and clear wrapped-token accounting.

item.title: Borrowing Stablecoins Against Wrapped XMR Requires a Live Market
item.description: Wrapped XMR can serve as collateral only where a live lending market accepts its token; bridging alone does not create a stablecoin loan, and liquidation can cost the XMR.

item.title: How to Consolidate Crypto Across Different Networks
item.description: Move assets to one chosen network by bridging or swapping across chains, while checking token versions, fees, liquidity and the destination address before signing.

item.title: Fermi swap: Three routes for treasury transfers
item.description: Fermi swap treasury routes range from a direct same-chain exchange to multi-hop and cross-chain paths, each adding execution steps, costs and settlement checks.

item.title: Check the destination chain before calling a bridge transfer complete
item.description: A bridge deposit is confirmed only when the destination chain records the transfer: check the right network, address, token contract and final transaction.

item.title: How NFT Ownership Moves Between Chains
item.description: NFTs can cross chains through coordinated burn-and-mint or lock-and-unlock contracts, but canonical ownership, metadata and failed-message recovery need explicit rules.

item.title: Three checks before canceling an omnichain request
item.description: Before canceling an omnichain request, check its chain status, whether destination execution has begun, and the fees or refund path tied to that route.

item.title: Four Checks Before You Mark a Cross-Chain Transfer Complete
item.description: A cross-chain transfer is done only when the destination chain records the expected asset at the intended address; check the route, receipt, amount and fees.

item.title: How to Fund Recurring Costs on a Low-Fee Chain
item.description: Recurring crypto costs work best when payment funds and gas stay on the same low-fee chain, with automation limited to amounts and schedules you can verify.

item.title: Where a Rango bridge swap can stall
item.description: A pending Rango bridge swap can pause before source confirmation, during cross-chain delivery or at destination execution; each stage points to a different next step.
